The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{1}{8},$ what is the value of $sec⁡\theta ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/4942cec8983dd2bddddd0ba2f8f9332b1b82f3999a44adb138b905457d39c633.png)

We're given that $y=\frac{1}{8}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, $sin⁡\theta =\frac{1}{8}.$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{1}{8}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{1}{8})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{64}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{63}{64}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{63}}{8} \\  & =\pm \frac{3\sqrt{7}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is negative in the second quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{8}.$

Finally, knowing that $sec⁡\theta =\frac{1}{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
sec⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(-\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{8})}=-\frac{8}{3\sqrt{7}}=-\frac{8\sqrt{7}}{21}.
$$
